newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares rise on peace hopes.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares rise on peace hopes.

text.p: Israeli shares closed broadly higher for the third consecutive session on Sunday on hopes of a breakthrough in Middle East peace talks, traders said.

The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.71 percent, or 4.29 points, to 255.69 on a high all-share turnover of 130 million shekels against 115 million shekels on Thursday, the last day of trading before the Israeli weekend.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 1.66 percent higher at 265.06.

"It's difficult to say why the market is rising since nothing fundamental has changed. I believe that the main reason is the improvement in investors' mood. There is a feeling that Netanyahu's visit to Washington would lead to a breakthrough in peace talks," said Doron Tsur, head of research at Sahar Securities.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu left on Sunday for crisis talks with U.S. President Bill Clinton on rescuing Middle East peace efforts.
Netanyahu hopes to get Clinton behind his offer to seal a final peace with the PLO in six months ending, if necessary, with an intensive U.S.-Israeli-PLO summit.

"There is no reason for optimism. It seems that Netanyahu would not offer any gestures on his trip. The only hope is that the Americans would force him to make a positive move. In such a case the market would start running," said a trader at Evergreen Capital Markets.
Tsur said the market was still attractive and share prices were relatively low.
"Moreover, fourth-quarter earning reports were above expectations. Despite that, the market is very volatile and it's impossible to say where it is going," Tsur added.

Blue Square Chain Stores Properties and Investments rose 1.75 percent to 3,410 agorot. Ofek Securities and Investments issued a "hold" recommendation for the company, saying an expected recession in Israel would affect it in 1997.

The most active shares were Bank Hapoalim which rose 2.25 percent to 706 agorot on volume of 9.2 million shekels, Israel Chemicals, which surged 4.25 percent to 391 agorot on turnover of 7.1 million shekels, and Teva Pharamceutical Industries, which rose 0.25 percent to 18,755 agorot on turnover of 5.4 million shekels.
